title: Abba Mari
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: “My father, my master”: this is how Rabbah son of Rav Huna was accustomed to speak when mentioning his father, who was his teacher, as in Gittin 29b and Sanhedrin 5a. Hyman says that Seder HaDorot thought it was the name of an Amora, and calls this “an error that issued from the ruler.”[^1][^2]

notes.text: Abba Mari is the address “my father, my master,” used by Rabbah bar Rav Huna in the William Davidson digital Gittin 29b and Sanhedrin 5a. Hyman’s objection to treating it as an independent personal name is his conclusion.

Gittin 29b and Sanhedrin 5a explicitly give Rabbah bar Rav Huna's expression Abba Mari, “my father, my master.” Hyman's criticism of treating it as an independent Amora's name remains his conclusion about the Seder HaDorot report; that work was not directly collated here. The expression is not promoted into a general identity rule.
